But the way he's doing it seems arrogant and hurtful. I feel guilty and bad about myself already, so his comments are making me feel worse. I used to be really into working out and had a healthy lifestyle, but after moving to a new city, I felt lonely and started eating a lot as a coping mechanism. I gained about 10 kilos in six months, which is a lot. My family has noticed, and I have acne because of the unhealthy food. The comments from my sister's husband are adding to my stress and making me feel even more isolated. I wonder if telling him off would help. On one hand, it might make me feel empowered because I'm standing up for myself. On the other hand, it could strain the relationship with my sister and her husband, which I don't want. Plus, maybe he doesn't realize how his words are affecting me. I should consider how to approach him. Maybe instead of calling him a jerk, I could explain how his comments make me feel. That way, he might understand and stop. But if I'm too hurt, maybe it's better to set boundaries or avoid him when he starts these conversations. I also need to think about my own well-being. I want to get back to a healthier lifestyle, but I'm feeling too tired and unmotivated. Maybe I can start small, like walking more or eating a bit healthier, and build up from there. Support from others would help, but if he's not supportive, I might need to find other ways to stay motivated. In the end, I have to decide what's best for me. If his comments are really affecting me negatively, then addressing it might be necessary. But I should do it in a way that's constructive, not confrontational, to maintain the relationship.
